questions.prompt: A readiness rule is enabled AND sensorHealthy. What is the result when enabled is true and sensorHealthy is false?
choices: true
false
It depends on the previous result
Java cannot evaluate it
questions.explanation: Both conditions must be true for an AND expression to be true.

questions.prompt: What does a DoubleSupplier such as () -> joystick.getY() let a command do?
choices: Read the joystick whenever the supplier is called
Read the joystick only when the supplier is created
Automatically reserve the drivetrain subsystem
Run the scheduler in a separate thread
questions.explanation: The callback is evaluated when called; a subsystem requirement must still be specified separately.

questions.prompt: Two interruptible commands require the same subsystem. If the second is scheduled while the first is running, what should you expect?
choices: Both normally control the subsystem at the same time
The first is interrupted and the second may take the requirement
The subsystem is permanently disabled
The first command finishes naturally before the second starts
questions.explanation: Under the normal interruptible behavior the scheduler interrupts the conflicting command. Commands can have different interruption policies, so inspect their configuration.

questions.prompt: When can a subsystem default command run?
choices: Only once at startup
When the subsystem is available and the scheduler schedules its default
While a conflicting command owns the same requirement
Only while the robot is powered off
questions.explanation: A default is scheduled when the subsystem is available; it yields to a command that requires that subsystem.

questions.prompt: With error defined as target minus measurement, previous error 1.0 m and current error 0.8 m after 0.1 s, what is the error derivative?
choices: +2 m/s
−2 m/s

questions.prompt: What can happen when a controller output is saturated while integral error continues to accumulate?
choices: Integral windup may delay recovery after the error changes
The integral term is guaranteed to remain zero
A motor gains unlimited torque
The sensor automatically recalibrates
questions.explanation: Integral windup can build up while the actuator cannot provide more output; limiting or resetting integral state may help.

questions.prompt: What is the role of a gravity feedforward term on an arm?
choices: Provide an estimated output to help counter gravity
Replace every sensor and safety limit
Measure the arm angle directly
Guarantee perfect tracking under any load
questions.explanation: Feedforward estimates an output needed for a known effect; feedback and safe limits still matter, and the estimate can be imperfect.

questions.prompt: Using +x forward, +y left and counterclockwise positive heading, what robot-relative vector corresponds to field-forward (1, 0) m/s when the robot heading is +90°?
questions.explanation: Rotate the field-relative vector by the negative heading: field-forward is robot-right at +90°, or (0, −1) m/s.

questions.prompt: An encoder measures 12 motor turns through a 6:1 motor-to-output reduction. Ignoring slip and sign, how many turns does the output make?
questions.explanation: A 6:1 motor-to-output reduction means six motor turns per output turn, so 12 / 6 = 2.

questions.prompt: Before a home reference is recorded, what does the encoder lab assume about its reference?
choices: It assumes zero reference turns; that does not prove physical home
It proves the mechanism is at its physical home switch
It reads a limit switch without wiring or simulation
It automatically knows the drum diameter
questions.explanation: The model assumes a zero reference until homing; a numerical zero alone is not evidence of the mechanism’s physical position.

questions.prompt: A camera observation arrives after a delay. Which time is needed to associate it with the robot state when the image was taken?
choices: The image capture timestamp
Only the time at which the dashboard displayed it
The scheduled end of the next match
The moment the code file was saved
questions.explanation: Capture and delivery times differ. Time-aware pose estimation needs a capture timestamp compatible with the estimator clock.

questions.prompt: A historical log shows an enable transition near a battery-voltage sample. What is supported by that proximity alone?
choices: The transition caused the voltage change
The two samples occurred near each other in recorded time
The robot won its match
The sampled voltage was the lowest voltage in the full log
questions.explanation: The samples have recorded times, but a causal claim requires additional context and evidence. Sparse sampling also can miss extrema.

questions.prompt: What should change when the same subsystem behavior runs against simulation instead of hardware?
choices: The implementation supplied through its IO interface
Every command and button binding
The meaning of radians per second
The command scheduler requirement rules
questions.explanation: An IO boundary lets behavior consume the same contract while real and simulated implementations obtain measurements and apply requests differently. The model still needs validation.

questions.prompt: In the training roller, a sample is read before the next voltage request is calculated. What does the sample describe?
choices: The future effect of the voltage about to be requested
The plant after the previously applied output interval
Proof that the real motor received its requested voltage
A prediction unaffected by timing
questions.explanation: The sample describes the plant after the prior output interval. The new output request affects the following interval; update ordering is part of the model contract.

questions.prompt: Which input must be reproducible to compare a replayed decision with the original decision?
choices: Only encoder position
Only the final output voltage
Every external input relevant to the decision, including requests and time
Only the robot class name
questions.explanation: A repeatable decision needs all relevant inputs, requests and timing. Replaying recorded sensor values does not guarantee that unlogged operator intent or wall-clock reads are reproduced.

questions.prompt: A table is validated only from 1 to 3 meters. Our CalibrationTable wrapper is queried at 4 meters. What happens?
choices: It proves the 3-meter value works at 4 meters
It extrapolates automatically
It returns OptionalDouble.empty() for the caller to handle
It inserts a new measured sample
questions.explanation: The teaching wrapper rejects queries outside its input domain. The underlying WPILib map instead clamps to an endpoint; neither behavior establishes that an unmeasured setting works physically.

questions.prompt: A speed sample is NaN but its timestamp is current. What should the validity check conclude?
choices: It is valid because it is fresh
It is invalid despite being fresh
It is a measured zero
A moving average guarantees a valid replacement
questions.explanation: Freshness and numerical validity are different checks. Do not turn an unknown measurement into a zero or assume that smoothing proves validity. Choose an explicit fault policy.

questions.prompt: Ready enters below 5 rad/s error and exits above 8 rad/s. If already ready and the error becomes 6 rad/s, what is the next state?
choices: Not ready
Ready, retaining the previous state between thresholds
Unknown regardless of sensor health
The error must be set to zero
questions.explanation: Hysteresis retains the prior state between entry and exit thresholds. This example assumes a valid measurement; handling stale or invalid measurements requires a separate explicit policy.
